g.text: but lifts its output per hour only about a tenth
The stages of an attack, the hours AI can take on, and the productivity gain by the end of 2026
Hour and AI shares are the author's judgements (bars show central ones). Productivity follows Amdahl's law: automating two-fifths
of the hours raises output per hour by at most ~60%, and only if AI did that work instantly and without error. The end-2026 figure
assumes a gang hands AI 10–80% of what it could do, that AI works 3–20 times faster, and that checking takes 10–40% as long as
doing the work by hand. Dots: medians; shaded bars: 80% ranges.
Sources: post-incident reports (Colonial Pipeline, Ireland's HSE, Change Healthcare, MGM, CDK Global); Conti and Black Basta chat
leaks; NCA; Sophos; Mandiant; Coveware; Chainalysis; GuidePoint; GreyNoise; Gambit Security; BakerHostetler; Anthropic and
Google threat reports; the author's earlier ransomware model; author's judgements and Monte Carlo model

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #121212

g.text: Together, AI can do about two-fifths of the hours (31–47%)
